title: Geometric relative module flatness is detected on any etale scheme atlas
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to T$ be an $S$-morphism to an $S$-scheme $T$, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and let $p:U\to X$ be any representable surjective etale morphism from a scheme. Use the canonical tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and let $F$ be the quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_U$-module corresponding to $p^*M$ under [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. For a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, put $\bar t=f\bar x$; write $M_{\bar x}$ and $\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$ for the stalks of the small etale module and structure sheaves, namely the colimits of their sections over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods. The following conditions are equivalent: (i) for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, the module $M_{\bar x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$ through the map induced by $f$; (ii) for every $u\in U$, with $t=fp(u)$, the ordinary Zariski stalk $F_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ through $\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\mathcal O_{U,u}$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Module flatness means [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. This equivalence holds for every such atlas; no finiteness, separation, Noetherian or flatness hypothesis on $f$ or $M$ is required.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, and put $\bar x=p\bar u$, $\bar t=f\bar x$, $u=|\bar u|$, $t=fp(u)$, $B=\mathcal O_{U,u}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}$. By [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness], applied to $p$ and to the identity chart of $T$, the natural germ maps identify $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ with $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$ with $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, using the residue embeddings specified by these geometric points. By [lem-sfb-space-quasicoherent-geometric-stalk-tensor], there is a canonical $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$-linear isomorphism $F_u\otimes_B B^{\mathrm{sh}}\simeq M_{\bar x}$. In particular it respects the $R$-action through $fp$: the two actions send each local function germ on $T$ to its pullback germ on the same pointed neighbourhood. Thus both are the restriction of the given $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-action.

source.place: Tag 05VU (lemma-flat-at-point), proof, with target chart V=T and source chart U.

proof.text: The map $B\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]. Apply [lem-trf-flatness-faithfully-flat-extension] to $R\to B\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and the $B$-module $F_u$. Using step 1 (and the tensor symmetry $b\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes b$, with inverse of the same form), it gives $F_u$ flat over $R$ if and only if $M_{\bar x}$ is flat over $R$. Apply [lem-sfb-strict-henselization-module-flatness] to the $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-module $M_{\bar x}$. This is equivalent to flatness over $R^{\mathrm{sh}}=\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$. This proves the desired equivalence for every chosen geometric lift $\bar u$, without a flatness assumption on $R\to B$.

proof.text: Assume (ii), and fix any $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$. Surjectivity of the atlas gives a point $u\in|U|$ over its image $x$; this is also the scheme-test meaning of surjectivity in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-sfb-etale-geometric-point-specified-lift], the etale map $p$ admits a lift $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over this specified $u$, with $p\bar u=\bar x$. Condition (ii) supplies flatness of $F_u$ over $R$. The equivalence of step 2 gives flatness of $M_{\bar x}$ over $\mathcal O_{T,f\bar x}$. Since $\bar x$ was arbitrary, (i) follows.

Assume (i), and let $u\in U$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(u)$, which exists by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The residue-field embedding defines a geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over $u$ by [def-weil-geometric-point]. Apply (i) to $\bar x=p\bar u$ and then step 2 to obtain that $F_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,fp(u)}$. This holds for every $u$, proving (ii). The same argument works for every given atlas. If $U$ is empty then surjectivity forces $X$ empty and both conditions are vacuous; the zero module and identity atlas also satisfy the argument unchanged.

lean.statement: theorem module_flat_iff_chart_stalk {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (T : Over S) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace T) (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.EtaleSite) (_hU : IsSurjective U.obj.hom) : (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk s) ⟶ X.obj.obj), Module.Flat (stalkRing s (x ≫ f.hom.hom)) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (stalkMap f s x)).obj ((stalkModel s x).modules.obj M))) ↔ ∀ u : X.etaleForget.obj U, Module.Flat (T.left.presheaf.stalk ((yoneda.preimage (U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom.hom)).left u)) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (((yoneda.preimage (U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom.hom)).left).stalkMap u).hom).obj ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor (X.etaleForget.obj U).toRingedSpace u).obj ((X.schemeRestriction U).obj M)))
lean.note: Geometric stalks and their scalar map use the existing normalized section-colimit model. The atlas is an arbitrary small-etale object with scheme-test surjectivity; its Zariski module is canonical restriction to opens, the inverse Zariski/etale comparison of its tensor pullback. The conclusion explicitly quantifies ordinary stalks and their canonical scalar restrictions.
